paper: An essential convex hull criterion for false confidence in location models
status: unrefereed candidate; written proofs; internal AI-assisted review only; no proof-assistant verification

definitions.hull: C_H is the closed convex hull of the essential support of H.
definitions.T: (T): liminf_{R->infinity} S(R)/g(R-b)=0 for every b>0; (T+) has the limit in place of the liminf.

claims.name: Lemma 0
claims.statement: Tail asymptotics: S(R) ~ c R^{d-p} exp(-R^p/p) for f_{p,d}; f_{p,d} satisfies (T+) for p>1 and fails (T) for 0<p<=1; g proportional to exp(-(1+r)log(1+r)) satisfies (T+) for d=1 and fails (T) for d>=2.
hypotheses: The stated radial densities on R^d.
claims.evidence: written proof; direction of tail ratios checked in code/verify_extensions.py

claims.name: Theorem 1
claims.statement: (a) theta not in int C_H implies H valid at theta. (b) Under (T), theta in int C_H implies liminf F(t)/t=0 as t->0, so (V) fails; under (T+), F(t)=o(t). (c) If (T) fails there is a bounded nonconvex open H valid at every parameter of C_H and every false parameter, so (T) is necessary for the equivalence.
hypotheses: Model (M): X=theta+AZ, posterior Q_x = law of x+AZ', A invertible, Z has density f(z)=g(|z|) on R^d with g positive, bounded and nonincreasing; flat prior, known shape, exact matching of sampling and posterior laws.
lambda_d(H)>0, H Lebesgue measurable.
Part (b) assumes (T); part (c) assumes (T) fails.
claims.evidence: written proof; finite Gaussian and exponential-power illustrations

claims.name: Corollary 2
claims.statement: A positive-measure H satisfies (V) at every theta not in H if and only if int C_H is contained in H.
hypotheses: Model (M): X=theta+AZ, posterior Q_x = law of x+AZ', A invertible, Z has density f(z)=g(|z|) on R^d with g positive, bounded and nonincreasing; flat prior, known shape, exact matching of sampling and posterior laws.
lambda_d(H)>0.

claims.name: Corollary 3
claims.statement: A nonempty open hypothesis, or a nonempty regular closed one, is valid at every false parameter if and only if it is convex.
hypotheses: Model (M): X=theta+AZ, posterior Q_x = law of x+AZ', A invertible, Z has density f(z)=g(|z|) on R^d with g positive, bounded and nonincreasing; flat prior, known shape, exact matching of sampling and posterior laws.
H nonempty open, or H the closure of its interior.

claims.name: Theorem 4
claims.statement: Four-way classification of the law of q_H(X) at each theta into Conservative, Anti-conservative, Crossing and Exact rows; Exact holds precisely when H agrees almost everywhere with a halfspace whose boundary passes through theta.
hypotheses: Model (M): X=theta+AZ, posterior Q_x = law of x+AZ', A invertible, Z has density f(z)=g(|z|) on R^d with g positive, bounded and nonincreasing; flat prior, known shape, exact matching of sampling and posterior laws.
(T); the o() statements need (T+).
H and its complement have positive measure.

claims.name: Corollary 5
claims.statement: If H and its complement are each valid at every parameter where they are false, H agrees almost everywhere with a halfspace. This is the corrected form of the conjecture of Martin (2024, Section 3); a ball is non-linear and valid at every false parameter.
hypotheses: Model (M): X=theta+AZ, posterior Q_x = law of x+AZ', A invertible, Z has density f(z)=g(|z|) on R^d with g positive, bounded and nonincreasing; flat prior, known shape, exact matching of sampling and posterior laws.
H and its complement have positive measure.

claims.name: Theorem 6
claims.statement: The posterior of a measurable real function phi is exact at every theta if and only if its sublevel sets are almost everywhere parallel halfspaces through theta; then phi=psi(a^T u) almost everywhere with psi strictly increasing.
hypotheses: Model (M): X=theta+AZ, posterior Q_x = law of x+AZ', A invertible, Z has density f(z)=g(|z|) on R^d with g positive, bounded and nonincreasing; flat prior, known shape, exact matching of sampling and posterior laws.
phi measurable.

claims.name: Theorem 7
claims.statement: log{F(t)/t}/(p log(1/t))^{(p-1)/p} tends to -rho as t->0, where rho is the signed shape-metric distance from theta to the boundary of C_H.
hypotheses: Model (M) with f=f_{p,d}, p>1.
H has positive measure and bounded essential support.
claims.evidence: written proof; finite-threshold tables in code/verify_examples.py and code/verify_exponential_power.py

claims.name: Theorem 8
claims.statement: If C is closed convex, H^c is contained in C almost everywhere, 0<s<1/2 and Q_theta(C)<=s, then P_theta{q_H(X)>=1-s}>=1/2; if C is also symmetric about theta this holds with probability one.
hypotheses: Model (M): X=theta+AZ, posterior Q_x = law of x+AZ', A invertible, Z has density f(z)=g(|z|) on R^d with g positive, bounded and nonincreasing; flat prior, known shape, exact matching of sampling and posterior laws.
f log-concave (covers f_{p,d} for p>=1).
claims.evidence: written proof; tested at each eligible entry of Table 2 in code/verify_extensions.py

claims.name: Proposition 9
claims.statement: Tail trichotomy for bounded hypotheses: for p>1 hull position decides; for 0<p<1, or p=1 and d>=2, F(t)/t tends to infinity at every theta; for p=1, d=1, F(t)=(t/2)(1/K_+ + 1/K_-) for small t, so hull position does not decide.
hypotheses: Model with f_{p,d} and A=I.
H has positive measure and bounded essential support.
claims.evidence: written proof; constant K checked in code/verify_extensions.py
